turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith stops just inside the door and doesn't sit. She sets her bag on the nearest desk and looks at her watch.

"I have until 4:40. You asked for this meeting, so I'll start with the basics.

Who decided to give Owen a zero? And did anyone speak to him before it went in the gradebook?"
Look, I'll own it if I messed up.

Meredith doesn't move.

"'If I messed up.'

That's a conditional. Is it your position that you might have, or that you don't know yet?

Either way, the zero is in the gradebook now. Owen read it on his phone in the middle of class. So I'll ask again: what was the basis for it, and who else has seen it?"

She pulls out a pen but doesn't open a notebook.

"I'll want the answer in an email, too."
Walk me through exactly what I did wrong with Owen's case. Step by step.

"You're asking me to build your file for you. Fine. Here's what I have.

One. The school's checker flagged the essay. That's a machine's opinion, and I know what those produce. I haven't seen the report.

Two. A zero went into the gradebook. As far as I can tell, that was before Owen was asked a single question.

Three. Owen found out on his phone, in class. No call to me. No conversation with him first.

Four. I don't know what policy you applied, or whether you followed it. That's your side to show me.

Five. Owen says he wrote it over the weekend. Did anyone ask him that before the zero went in?"

She looks up.

"Correct me on any of it. Which of those did I get wrong?"
